prediction.likelyOutcome: Liability on the underlying breach is roughly a coin flip given the pre-COVID October 2019 default, but if the Developers prevail (or substantially prevail) on waiver/estoppel grounds, the court is far more likely to award the well-documented Tower/Theater reliance damages (~$8.6M) than the roughly $11M in speculative garage lost-profit/NPV projections or the unquantified garage-completion and ancillary categories, which face serious new-business-rule and causation problems. Net recovery, if any, is likely to land well below the Developers' full trial ask and concentrated in the reliance-damages categories, discounted meaningfully for the real chance the City prevails on liability and its counterclaim given the pre-pandemic deadline miss.

outcome.description: After an October 2022 bench trial the district court found the City breached the Development Agreement (and tortiously interfered with the construction loan) and awarded Parking LLC $4,353,677 in expectancy damages (garage development fee, savings under the stipulated price, and interest) against the City, rejecting all other claimed damages and the City's counterclaims; court costs were taxed to the City. The Iowa Supreme Court affirmed the breach-of-contract judgment and the $4,353,677 award on June 12, 2026, vacated the tortious-interference judgment, and affirmed the denial of the Developers' additional damages.
outcome.finalNote: Damages affirmed; tortious-interference liability vacated without changing the amount.
